title: cold-start-mitigation-private-deployments-arch-meeting-notes
content:
Meeting: Architecture review — Cold-start mitigation for Private Deployments
Date: 2025-10-07 10:00-11:30 PT
Facilitator: Aisha Khatri
Attendees: Aisha K., Ethan M., Priya S., Jon P., Marta L., Samira (security), Theo (solutions eng)

Purpose / Background:
- Repeated customer reports of high p95/p99 latency during first request bursts after autoscale events and node restarts in Private (VPC/on-prem) installs.
- Root causes observed in earlier study: model weights loading from slow NFS, KMS decrypt latency when keys are remote, JIT/kernel cold paths, and large first-token KV-cache overhead.
- Dedicated (hosted) mitigations (prewarmed pools) exist but are not directly portable to Private due to resource constraints, network variability, and stricter KMS policies.

Agenda:
1) Quick recap of telemetry and customer impact (Ethan)
2) Short proposals (A/B/C) for mitigation (Priya)
3) Security & compliance constraints for KMS handling (Samira)
4) Cost / ops tradeoffs and rollout plan (Marta + Theo)
5) Decisions and owners

Telemetry recap (Ethan):
- Topline: p95 cold-start latency for private nodes observed in field: median 3.2s, p95 9.8s, p99 23s for text-generation API first request after pod start.
- Breakdown from tracing spans (sampled): 40% weight load (I/O unpack + mmap), 30% KMS unwrap/blocking handshake, 20% kernel init / CUDA context warm, remainder tokenization & kv-cache population.
- Higher variance on setups with NFS-backed model stores and when KMS is proxied over inter-region links.
- INF-2187 has detailed traces and heap profiles.

Proposals discussed:
- Proposal A: Minimal-invasive prewarm shim (low-effort)
  - On node startup, run a lightweight warmup job that: pulls model artifact to tmpfs, performs a one-shot key unwrap/keepalive, executes a single short prompt to trigger kernel paths (dummy tokens), then exits.
  - Implementation: init container + Kubernetes Job per node for private clusters; on-prem package: a systemd unit that runs the same flow.
  - Pros: low engineering surface, limited resource usage, aligns with existing prewarm pattern in Hosted.
  - Cons: needs disk tmpfs capacity, KMS credentials available at bootstrap (security questions), still incurs full weight unpack for large model (though subsequent requests faster).

- Proposal B: Snapshot-based restore (more invasive)
  - Create serialized runtime snapshot (cold checkpoint) of model in memory after warmup; store snapshot as compressed artifact in model-store. At node startup, mmap snapshot into process address space and resume, bypassing full init.
  - Implementation: extend model artifact packaging to include snapshot blob; runtime loads snapshot via optimized mmap and memory remapping. Requires format design and portability testing across kernel/GPU driver versions.
  - Pros: considerably lower startup time in test runs (p95 drops to ~1.2s), reduced repeated KMS unwraps if snapshot contains unwrapped keys (see security tradeoffs).
  - Cons: complex, brittle across OS/kernel/GPU driver differences, larger storage footprint, potential security concerns if keys or secrets embedded.

- Proposal C: Two-tier warm pool + adaptive lazy-loading (hybrid)
  - Maintain a tiny hot pool of lightweight worker processes per node with only kernel/JIT warmed (weights on demand). For very cold requests, route to a 'slow' path and return a 202-accepted + callback pattern (or stream warm response when ready). Implement background streaming warm-up that fetches weights and populates KV cache after initial handshake.
  - Implementation: small runtime refactor, route policy changes in smart-router, API contract decision for 202/streaming.
  - Pros: avoids storing big snapshots, limits upfront cost, gives graceful degradation for heavy models.
  - Cons: requires API UX changes (202 path), more complex traffic routing and client expectations, may break backward compatibility if not careful.

Security & Compliance considerations (Samira):
- KMS unwrap: key material must not be persisted in plaintext in snapshot artifacts. Snapshots that embed unwrapped keys are a hard no for enterprise customers unless protected by HSM-bound secrets and explicit opt-in.
- Init-time KMS handshake allowed, but must be auditable and follow customer policy (no long-lived decrypted keys on disk).
- Proposal B currently assumes snapshot might include wrapped-secret cache — must be redesigned to store only sealed blobs using node-local KMS/HSM or use ephemeral session tokens.
- Action: produce threat model for snapshot format if we pursue B (Samira + Priya). Due: 2025-10-17.

Performance estimates (benchmarks from lab runs Priya presented):
- Baseline cold p95 (no mitigation): 9.8s
- A (init container warmup): p95 2.6s, median 1.0s, memory overhead ~200MB tmpfs per model pulled
- B (snapshot prototype, lab on Ubuntu 24): p95 1.1s, median 0.7s, storage delta +700MB per model artifact
- C (hybrid warm pool + lazy): p95 3.5s for first interactive response, median 0.9s for subsequent; smoother tail but requires client change for first request in worst-case
- Note: lab numbers exclude KMS network anomalies. When KMS latency simulated +500ms, A increases by ~400ms, B unaffected if no unwrap needed, C depends on route.

Operational / Cost tradeoffs (Marta + Theo):
- A: easiest to roll, cost proportional to tmpfs and pull bandwidth during scale events. For large fleets, frequent cold starts will spike network egress and model-store IOPS.
- B: cost in storage and potential ops complexity (compatibility matrix). But reduces repeated pulls over time. Snapshot publish will add pipeline steps and QA checks.
- C: adds complexity to router; human-facing clients might need documentation for 202/streaming UX. More maintainable if we can avoid carrying unwrapped secrets.

Decision (consensus):
- Short-term (Q4 immediate): implement Proposal A as the quick mitigation for Private deployments with an init-container / systemd warmup job. Start rolling to customers with an opt-in config flag: "enable_coldstart_prewarm". Goal: reduce p95 within 2 weeks of patch rollout. (Owner: Priya; PR: GH #492)
- Mid-term (Q1 planning): prototype Proposal B as an experimental opt-in pipeline for large models (>=30GB). Focus on read-only snapshot format that explicitly excludes any unwrapped key material; instead rely on node-local sealing using customer KMS/HSM when available. Produce threat model and compatibility matrix first. (Owner: Jon + Samira; JIRA: INF-2187-B)
- Long-term: evaluate hybrid Proposal C dependent on API UX decision and product acceptance. Consider streaming-first API for very large models; product to run customer interviews before committing. (Owner: Theo + Product)

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Q1: For Proposal A, what happens if tmpfs fills or node has constrained memory? We need a fallback (use disk + throttle). (Owner: Priya; Due: 2025-10-14)
- Q2: Snapshot portability across container runtimes and GPU drivers — narrow supported matrix and document it. (Owner: Jon; Due: 2025-11-05)
- Q3: For customers using on-prem HSMs, how do we key-wrap snapshots? Define processes and docs. (Owner: Samira; Due: 2025-10-17)
- Q4: Observability: new spans for warmup job and responsibility for alerting (we need an alert: frequent prewarm failures >5% in 5m). (Owner: Ethan + SRE; Due: 2025-10-13)

Action items (explicit):
- Priya: implement init-container warmup flow, include tmpfs fallback to disk, add config flag and Helm values. Target PR and internal dogfood 2025-10-20.
- Jon: design snapshot metadata format draft, research mmap compatibility constraints across kernels and container runcs. Deliver doc: 2025-10-31.
- Samira: threat model for snapshot format; guidance for HSM usage and no-plaintext guarantee. Deliver: 2025-10-17.
- Ethan: add warmup job telemetry spans and create an SLO/alert prototype. Deliver: 2025-10-13.
- Marta/Theo: compile rollout plan and cost estimate for both A and B; include customer comms template for opt-in. Deliver: 2025-10-24.

Notes / small ideas shelved for now:
- Using a tiny quantized stub model to answer initial queries while the full model loads (interesting but shifts quality profile; leave for model-team exploration).
- Heuristic: keep most-requested models prewarm-enabled by default for high-usage tenants. Blacklist for low-memory customers.

Appendix: quick links and snippets
- Local test script used by Priya: repo/runtime/tools/warmup-scripts/warmup-job.sh
- Sample Helm flag: values.serving.prewarm.enabled=true
- Lab benchmark run: GH #492 bench branch output: /artifacts/bench/coldstart/2025-10-06/summary.md

Meeting notes captured by: Aisha Khatri
Next sync: follow-up review 2025-10-21 10:00 PT (status on A rollout + snapshot feasibility).

Informal notes / scribbles (copied from whiteboard, unpolished):
- "If KMS is the tail, make KMS async and cache tokens short-lived locally" — but careful with audit.
- "Snapshot without keys; re-wrap with node-local key on first boot" might be workable with HSM.
- "Users will hate 202 unless we give a seamless streaming UX"

End of doc.
